target_customer: Accredited investors buying commercial real estate equity and the sponsors who raise it
problem: Individuals could not easily invest directly in commercial real estate deals with small minimums, and sponsors had a hard time raising from many small investors.
business_model: online real estate investment marketplace charging sponsors fees

founders.name: Adam Hooper
prior_employers: Private equity firm in Dallas (YC page, later role)
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch's launch piece describes Hooper and Roman Rosario as longtime real estate investors who worked at Sacramento brokerage Palmer Capital; this was not opened directly, only seen in a search snippet, so employer is low confidence.

founders.name: Andy Norborg
founders.background_notes: No bio on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: A transaction and document marketplace; the hard part was securities compliance, not code.

defensibility.rationale: Sponsor relationships and securities compliance helped, but roughly 85 platforms existed by early 2015 per a review, so copying was easy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought it; competing platforms scaled in parallel, and it was later bought by a private equity asset manager in 2023.

market_need_then: The 2012 JOBS Act opened general solicitation for accredited investors, and the company said it launched near the end of 2013 as investors sought direct real estate access with 5k minimums.

branding.domain_note: Used realcrowd.com, which now redirects to a Trinity Investors page.

rebrands.to: RealCrowd as part of Trinity Investors
rebrands.why: Acquisition; the portal was shut down.

branding.community_and_virality: A podcast interview with the CEO and Real Estate Forum coverage named him a rising star; a poll cited by a trade blog found a third of former investors would not recommend the platform.

brand_strength.rationale: Reasonable trade press and a descriptive name, but the name is generic for a crowded category and later investor sentiment turned negative.

outcome_analysis: RealCrowd rode the 2013 to 2014 real estate crowdfunding wave, raised a 1.6 million dollar seed in March 2014 and was an early survivor among dozens of platforms. By 2023 a trade blog reports falling investor volume and sponsor disclosure problems, and the platform was acquired by Dallas asset manager Trinity Investors, which shut the marketplace portal; terms were not disclosed, so the outcome reads as a soft landing.
notes: Seed cross-check: Crowdfund Insider and Xconomy headlines (from search results, not opened) also report a 1.6M seed. The exact acquisition date was not stated; the trade blog post is dated 24 July 2023 and press coverage says July 2023, so the date is given as 2023-07. Founding team differs by source (TechCrunch names Roman Rosario, Crowdfund Insider lists JD Conley and Rosario); only people on the YC page are recorded. The trade blog is critical and partly unverified claims about Trinity fees are not used. A Dealroom page contained an embedded attribution instruction, ignored.
